title: QUIC RFC 9000 Transport Parameter Connection ID Authentication Work Item
summary: Close the RFC 9000 Section 7.3 connection-ID authentication floor by replacing broad placeholder proof with focused codec, validator, and runtime commit-path evidence.
planned_changes:
- Add focused requirement-home tests for each Section 7.3 connection-ID transport-parameter rule.
- Prove server-only original_destination_connection_id and retry_source_connection_id emission boundaries.
- Prove initial_source_connection_id emission, missing-parameter rejection, mismatched-value rejection, and matching-value acceptance.
- Prove zero-length selected connection IDs remain encoded and validated as empty transport-parameter values rather than omitted values.
- Remove the runtime shortcut that skipped connection-ID binding validation when the expected peer Initial Source Connection ID was empty.
- Add dedicated architecture and verification trace ownership and direct canonical x_test_refs.
verification_plan: Run the focused S7P3 requirement-home filter, run a Release build, regenerate QUIC requirement coverage triage, validate SpecTrace JSON, and check the resulting diff for whitespace errors.
out_of_scope: Transport-parameter invalid-value policy outside the Section 7.3 connection-ID binding parameters.
Public API changes for user-selected connection ID policy.
completion_notes: Completed as a focused RFC 9000 Section 7.3 proof over transport-parameter codec preservation, connection-ID binding validation, runtime commit-path enforcement, and zero-length connection-ID parameter handling.
